 (Correction: A previous e-mail included information from a previous week. Seeking Alpha regrets the error.) 

Wall Street’s major indexes mostly lost ground this week due to a persistent technology trade selloff and climbing oil prices.

 The technology and communications giant Meta ( META ) declined 8.3% this week after it reported its third quarter earnings, which showed a $9.9B litigation charge, elevated capital expenditures, and guidance that exposed the scale of the company's ongoing AI infrastructure buildout.

 Among notable technology companies declining this week were CoreWeave ( CRWV ) -9.4% this week, Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ) -8.7%, Synopsys ( SNPS ) -7.1%, keysight Technologies ( KEYS ) -5.9%, and Teradyne ( TER ) -5%.

 Also affecting the markets was the rising price of oil. Oil prices rose after reports that the U.S. and Israel could be drawing plans to attack Iran as the war in the Middle East intensifies.

 Crude oil futures ( CL1:COM ) rose to $103, up 1.8% this week, while Brent ( CO1:COM ) was also higher at $116 per barrel, up 6.2% this week.

 Moreover, U.S. Treasury yields saw big swings this week amid a market rotation away from tech equities as AI expenditures dragged investor sentiment. Traders pulled away from tech and flocked to Treasuries, triggering the largest flight in recent years.

 Bond prices rose, and the Treasuries such as the 10-year yield ( US10Y ) declined -1.6% this week to 5.00%. The 30-year yield ( US30Y ) also declined 1.8% to 5.33%, while the 2-year yield ( US2Y ) dropped 0.4% to 4.70%.

 In economic news, the October U.S. PMI Composite fell to 57.6, as expected, according to S&P Global on Friday. In addition, the U.S. Manufacturing PMI rose higher than consensus, while the U.S. Services PMI was slightly lower than expected.

 Also, housing starts unexpectedly fell in September, while building permits held up. Pending home sales dropped 7.3% in September more than expected.

 For the week, the S&P ( SP500 ) lost 0.5%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( COMP:IND ) was 0.7% lower, and the blue-chip Dow ( DJI ) gained 0.4%. Read a preview of next week's major events in Seeking Alpha's Catalyst Watch .


 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Outlook
 
 
 
 'Wrecking ball' 
 
 
 
Seeking Alpha
 
 
The UN is sounding the alarm on this year's El Niño, with the agency's emergency relief chief Tom Fletcher describing it as "a wrecking ball" that will bring extreme heat, droughts and floods. While El Niño is a normal climate pattern, it's expected to be unprecedented this year. This year appears similar to the 1997-98 event that caused an estimated $5.7T in global income losses. Read more. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Seeking Alpha's Calls Of The Week
 
 
 
Upgrading AppLovin ( APP ): Stock Has Fallen Too Far .

Papa John's ( PZZA ): Reset Paves Way For Recovery .

Patient Traders Can Start Buying  Winnebago ( WGO ).

 CII's  Distribution Is Likely Covered Through 2027 .

 RWTQ  Is Priced For Default, It's  Time To Buy .

Netflix ( NFLX ): I Was So Wrong, I Want To Cry .

Realty Income ( O ) May Be In Trouble, I'm Holding .

Red Cat's ( RCAT ) Steyr Deal Raises Dilution Risk .

AeroVironment ( AVAV ) Still Overvalued: It's A 'Sell.' 

Wynn Resorts ( WYNN ): Macau Weakness Persists .
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 U.S. Indices 
Dow +0.4% to 52,215. S&P 500 -0.5% to 7,624. Nasdaq -0.7% to 25,955. Russell 2000 +2% to 2,776. CBOE Volatility Index -2.7% to 19.45. 

 S&P 500 Sectors 
Consumer Staples +0.5%. Utilities +0.8%. Financials +0.7%. Telecom -6.2%. Healthcare +1.5%. Industrials -1.9%. Information Technology -0.3%. Materials -0.1%. Energy +1.6%. Consumer Discretionary +0.5%. Real Estate +1.1%. 

 World Indices 
London -1.8% to 10,690. France -2.2% to 7,783. Germany -1.7% to 25,182. Japan -4% to 62,693. China -0.7% to 3,690. Hong Kong -4.5% to 23,093. India -2.2% to 73,124. 

 Commodities and Bonds 
Crude Oil WTI +4.5% to $103.44/bbl. Gold -4.1% to $4,010./oz. Natural Gas -15.6% to 2.63. Ten-Year Bond Yield -0.2 bps to 4.988. 

 Forex and Cryptos 
EUR/USD -0.33%. USD/JPY -0.74%. GBP/USD +0.36%. Bitcoin -0.8%. Litecoin -2.7%. Ethereum -0.8%. XRP -0.1%. 

 Top S&P 500 Gainers 
Hashbro ( HAS ) +19%. Charles River Laboratories ( CRL ) +15%. Roper Technologies ( ROP ) +14%. Allegion ( ALLE ) +14%. CrowdStrike Holdings ( CRWD ) +13%. 

 Top S&P 500 Losers 
Comfort Systems USA ( FIX ) -19%. Howmet Aerospace ( HWM ) -16%. Flex ( FLEX ) -15%. Quanta Services ( PWR ) -14%. Lam Research ( LRCX ) -13%.
